title: Bounded Rationality in Central Bank Communication
abstract: arXiv:2411.04286v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This study explores the influence of FOMC sentiment on market expectations, focusing on cognitive differences between experts and non-experts. Using sentiment analysis of FOMC minutes, we integrate these insights into a bounded rationality model to examine the impact on inflation expectations. Results show that experts form more conservative expectations, anticipating FOMC stabilization actions, while non-experts react more directly to inflation concerns. A lead-lag analysis indicates that institutions adjust faster, though the gap with individual investors narrows in the short term. These findings highlight the need for tailored communication strategies to better align public expectations with policy goals.

translated_title: 央行沟通中的有限理性
translated_abstract: 本研究探讨美联储公开市场委员会（FOMC）情绪对市场预期的影响，重点关注专家与非专家之间的认知差异。通过对FOMC会议纪要进行情感分析，我们将这些洞察融入一个有限理性模型，以检验其对通胀预期的影响。结果表明，专家形成的预期更为保守，会预判FOMC的稳定化行动，而非专家则对通胀担忧做出更直接的反应。领先-滞后分析显示，机构调整速度更快，但短期内与个人投资者之间的差距会缩小。这些发现凸显了制定量身定制的沟通策略的必要性，以便更好地使公众预期与政策目标保持一致。
tldr: 本研究通过情感分析与有限理性模型揭示了专家与非专家对FOMC沟通的认知差异——专家预期更保守并预判央行的稳定化行动，非专家则对通胀担忧反应更直接——表明央行需要制定差异化的沟通策略以协调公众预期与政策目标。
en_tdlr: This study reveals systematic cognitive differences between experts and non-experts in interpreting FOMC communication—experts form more conservative expectations anticipating stabilization actions while non-experts react directly to inflation concerns—highlighting the need for tailored central bank communication strategies to align public expectations with policy goals.
